Transform the reference photogrammetry plate into a razor-sharp, photorealistic architectural survey image.

1. PLANAR RECTIFICATION & GEOMETRY LOCK: Treat the reference image as an immutable spatial coordinate frame. Eliminate all 3D mesh polygon wobble, melted facades, and distorted rooflines. 2. STATIC DECLUTTERING (MANDATORY): COMPLETELY ERASE all transient vehicles, parked cars, delivery vans, pedestrians, and temporary street clutter from the seed image. Repaint the ground plane with the authentic surfacing, kerbs, and pavement named in the SCENE section below.
3. BOTANICAL PHENOLOGY & CANOPY INTEGRITY: Overwrite all raw 3D mesh blob foliage with authentic seasonal canopy structures matching the target date. Zero green summer foliage during dormant/autumn/winter periods:
   Vegetation reflects late-summer phenology on September 4. Canopy composition features mature *Ulmus americana* (American elm) forming dense vaulted canopies with deep green foliage showing localized chlorosis along leaf margins; *Quercus palustris* (pin oak) and *Quercus alba* (white oak) with fully expanded, dark green coriaceous leaves; *Prunus serrulata* (Yoshino cherry) groupings showing late-season foliar fatigue and subtle foliage thinning; *Acer rubrum* (red maple) with incipient anthocyanin accumulation on terminal leaf sprays; and *Platanus × acerifolia* (London planetree) displaying peeling cream-olive bark plates beneath mature lobed leaves. Manicured turf consists of dense *Festuca arundinacea* (tall fescue) and *Poa pratensis* (Kentucky bluegrass) showing high-traffic compaction patterns along path margins.
4. OPTICAL DEPTH: Sharp focus across the entire frame, near to far. No blur, no depth-of-field falloff, no vignetting.

[SOLAR & ATMOSPHERIC LIGHTING OVERRIDE]
SOLAR RELIGHTING DIRECTIVE (4500K Late afternoon raking sunlight with warm golden highlights):
- SUN POSITION IN SCREEN SPACE: Sun is ahead and to the LEFT, in the upper-left background (True Azimuth 267.1°, Elevation 15.3°).
- FACADE ILLUMINATION: all camera-facing facades are in shadow, reading as backlit silhouettes with a bright rim along their sunward edges; left-facing walls are brightly lit and right-facing walls are in deep shadow.
- CAST SHADOW DIRECTION: cast shadows project diagonally toward the camera and to the lower-RIGHT.
- CAST SHADOW LENGTH: Every cast shadow is 3.6 times as long as the height of the object casting it. A 100 m tower casts a 364 m shadow. Apply this ratio to every object in the scene.
- SHADOW OVERWRITE RULE: MANDATORY: Erase every cast shadow present in the reference plate before relighting. Render all previously shadowed ground and facades as if that shadow never existed, then cast entirely new shadows so that cast shadows project diagonally toward the camera and to the lower-RIGHT. Every shadow must be angled toward the RIGHT; a shadow running straight up or straight down the frame is wrong. Do not retain, tint, or reuse any shadow from the reference plate.
- WEATHER/SKY: Crisp clear sky with direct solar exposure.

[SCENE GEOMETRY & AUTHENTIC LITHICS]
Washington Monument obelisk of load-bearing dressed calcitic Cockeysville marble ashlar, showing a distinct horizontal material transition line at forty-six meters between lower Symington quarry courses and upper Beaver Dam marble blocks, capped by an eight-sided marble pyramidion. Concentric plaza of thermal-finished Rockville white granite flagstones with stainless steel flagpoles mounted in circular granite coping. National Museum of African American History and Culture featuring a three-tiered inverted ziggurat corona clad in porous ornamental cast-aluminum panels with bronze-colored fluoropolymer coating over clear structural curtain-wall glazing and a polished black granite water-table base. Surrounding civic edifices of smooth-dressed Indiana Bedford limestone ashlar, rusticated granite foundations, repetitive fenestration grids of multi-pane bronze sashes, and patinated copper mansards. Curvilinear walkways of compacted tan decomposed granite aggregate bounded by granite stone curbs. Mature *Ulmus americana* trees with dense dark-green canopies showing early September late-summer chlorosis, alongside *Quercus palustris*, *Platanus × acerifolia*, and *Prunus serrulata* groves with heavy foliar density. Extensive swathes of *Festuca arundinacea* turf cut by precise radial path geometries and manicured earth berms.
